author: MiniMax Agent
description: VORTEX-OS is a self-bootstrapping PowerShell skill that drives the .NET 10 C++/CLI engine at Cloudmeru/vortex-os-dotnet to orchestrate multi-agent work pipelines with strict continuity enforcement, self-healing prompts, and explicit Human-in-the-Loop approval. The engine decomposes a master objective into a 4-tier chain of command (planner → supervisor → shift → specialized workers), runs the workers in parallel across distinct domains, auto-rewrites any prompt that violates a continuity rule, gates high-stakes actions behind explicit human approval, and writes a fully-attributed audit log. Use it for: multi-domain work (3+ deliverable types in one pipeline), universe/character/era continuity enforcement, explicit HITL approval on high-stakes actions, per-agent audit trails, long-running/episodic/series scope, in-house execution without external API dependencies. Do NOT use it for: single-line code questions, pure chat, single-file edits with no cross-domain coordination, read-only research, or tasks with no clear objective.

flow: User runs `pwsh -NoProfile -File skill.ps1 <args>` from the skill folder.
skill.ps1 searches $env:VORTEX_MODULE_PATH, $env:PSModulePath, and $HOME\Documents\PowerShell\Modules for an installed Vortex.<version>\Vortex.psd1.
If not found, skill.ps1 calls install.ps1, which downloads the 4 engine files from the public GitHub release of Cloudmeru/vortex-os-dotnet.
install.ps1 places the files in the first writable user-scope module folder (canonical: $HOME\Documents\PowerShell\Modules\Vortex\<version>\).
skill.ps1 sets $env:VORTEX_SKILL_ROOT to the skill folder so the engine finds agents/ + state/.
skill.ps1 imports the module and dispatches the command. Exit code from the engine is exposed via Get-VortexLastExitCode and used as the script's exit code.

name: VORTEX-OS

winget_install_ids.name: sqlite3
winget_install_ids.description: SQLite CLI (used by the engine's VectorHydrate for memory persistence). If missing, the engine skips memory persistence and writes a schema file instead.

winget_install_ids.name: ffmpeg
winget_install_ids.description: Audio/video processor. Not used by the engine itself, but required by generated *audio deliverables* (Foley, sample chopping, DSP). Install only if you plan to generate audio deliverables.

install_fallbacks.description: v0.2.3 (G10): if winget is not installed (older Windows, locked-down corporate machines, missing App Installer), install-deps.ps1 walks this list in order and uses the first one that exists. The 'direct' entry is a static URL the operator can paste into a browser; the script will also offer to download + unzip it.

requirements.winget_install_note: The engine is pure .NET 10 / C++/CLI. It does NOT need Python, jq, or any scripting runtime. All system deps install via Windows Package Manager (winget) — never pip/brew/apt. Use the bundled install-deps.ps1 to install. If winget is unavailable, the script falls back to choco, scoop, or a direct download (see install_fallbacks).

data_location.description: Starting with engine v0.1.7 + skill v0.1.4, the engine splits storage into a mutable skill folder and a durable VORTEX_HOME. The user's deliverables, audit log, swarms, and HITL state live in VORTEX_HOME so they survive skill updates and are shared across multiple skill instances on the same machine.
data_location.migration_strategy: manual via migrate-state.ps1 (not auto-migrated by the engine)

auto_update.description: Starting with skill v0.1.5, skill.ps1 checks for a newer vortex-os-dotnet release on GitHub on every invocation and installs it if available. Rate-limited to once per 6h per VORTEX_HOME.

Engine v0.1.7+ writes state to $env:VORTEX_HOME (default %APPDATA%\Vortex-OS) so outputs survive skill updates; engine v0.1.8+ groups deliverables by project name; skill v0.1.5+ auto-updates the engine on every invocation (rate-limited, opt-out).
